consumption_180d.event: real personal consumption is higher at the horizon than at the origin
consumption_180d.label: real consumption (180d)
consumption_180d.rationale: the collective layer's central claim is that households defer spending before the aggregates show it; this is where that claim is most directly testable

consumption_360d.event: real personal consumption is higher at the horizon than at the origin
consumption_360d.label: real consumption (360d)

credit_stress_180d.event: credit card delinquency is higher at the horizon than at the origin
credit_stress_180d.label: credit stress (180d)
credit_stress_180d.rationale: delinquency is a lagging record of a decision made months earlier, so anything that leads it is genuinely early information

credit_stress_360d.event: credit card delinquency is higher at the horizon than at the origin

housing_180d.event: housing starts are higher at the horizon than at the origin
housing_180d.label: housing activity (180d)
housing_180d.rationale: Section 21's consensus-attacking case: rate cuts are supposed to revive housing, and the alternative is that insecurity blocks the transmission

housing_360d.event: housing starts are higher at the horizon than at the origin

industrial_180d.event: industrial production is higher at the horizon than at the origin
industrial_180d.label: industrial production (180d)
industrial_180d.rationale: a downstream test: household behaviour reaching manufacturing through orders should be slower and weaker than the direct consumption channel, and if it is not, something is wrong

industrial_360d.event: industrial production is higher at the horizon than at the origin

labour_180d.event: the unemployment rate is higher at the horizon than at the origin
labour_180d.label: labour deterioration (180d)
labour_180d.rationale: workers' read of their own options is hypothesised to move before the unemployment rate does; if it does not, perceived_control is a labour statistic wearing a psychological name
